title: COMP 4736 · Part 2
subtitle: OS structures (monolithic, layered, microkernel, client-server, virtual machines) and clocks (hardware, one-shot and square-wave modes, the clock driver's six duties)
description: Part 2 of Rahim Oraji's lectures (Tanenbaum Ch. 1 and 5): the six structures on the agenda and the five taught; the monolithic main program / service procedures / utility procedures with Linux's loadable modules and the hello-world kernel module; Dijkstra's THE layers and MS-DOS; microkernels and MINIX 3; the client-server model; virtual machines, VM/370 with CMS, type 1 and type 2 hypervisors with ESXi and VirtualBox; then clocks: crystal, counter and holding register, one-shot versus square-wave mode, the 500 MHz → 2 nsec → 8.6 sec arithmetic, the clock driver's six duties, time of day in ticks (overflows in 2.274 years) or seconds (136 years), the quantum counter, CPU accounting, the alarm linked list 3 → 4 → 6 → 2 → 1, and watchdog timers. Playback animations for the programmable clock and the alarm list. Ends with a mock midterm section and the closed-book recall drill.
intro:
:::quiz What the exam asks here
Structure questions are definitions and examples (which structure runs most of the OS as user processes; which OS is monolithic; what a type 1 hypervisor runs on). Clock questions are arithmetic: period = 1/f, the largest interval a 32-bit counter can time, the value to load for a quantum, when a tick counter overflows, and the next-signal list. Show the formula and the units on paper.
:::
